title: Selected contextual review across platforms
selection_scope: 28 additional records; alongside, not a replacement for, the earlier 22-post log. Selection is by documented subject and available sources, not a scale of prophetic fit.
interpretation_attribution: Micah Blumberg's existing First Beast and Antichrist interpretation supplies the research questions. New event-specific author annotations remain unset.
psychology_scope: Public self-presentation, appeals to an audience, stated demands, promised benefits and threatened consequences are observable textual subjects. No diagnosis, private mental-state inference, or prophetic-identity verdict is assigned.
source_access_default: Relevant passage and surrounding text consulted in the cited public transcript; not a native-platform capture or verification of every claim in the document.

sources.title: Turning Point USA Teen Student Action Summit
UPI report of December 3 statement
sources.access_note: Report quotes the post. Its page was updated December 4. Original platform identifier and exact timestamp are not recovered here.

sources.title: UPI report of December 5 response
sources.access_note: Report quotes the follow-up and earlier wording; no original platform capture is claimed.

sources.title: Archived CPAC video post
sources.access_note: The archive transcript and original URL were consulted. The complete video was not independently watched or transcribed. Capture date is later than the post date.

sources.title: CNN transcript of the Hannity town-hall clip
sources.access_note: A December 6 rush transcript quotes the December 5 Fox town hall. The complete original town hall was not independently reviewed; broadcaster commentary is not adopted.

sources.title: Archived January 14 video post
sources.access_note: Archive identifies original post at 10:39 PM EST and supplies a video transcript. Narration is distinguished from words spoken by Trump; original video bytes were not captured.

sources.title: AFP report of post after assassination attempt
sources.access_note: AFP syndication quotes the post and its unity appeal. The native post ID and exact timestamp remain unrecovered.

sources.title: AP: White House clarification concerning SNAP
sources.access_note: Consulted the report of the White House clarification, not every event in the live-news collection.

records.title: Personal indispensability
records.quote: I alone can fix it.
records.summary: The nomination speech presents Trump as able to repair a system he describes as rigged.
records.context: The same speech promises collaboration with prosecutors, police and allies. This is also the existing wiki's 2016 example, not a newly discovered event.
records.research_question: What authority is claimed for the speaker, and what later conduct makes support conditional?

records.title: News organizations described as an enemy
records.quote: it is the enemy of the American People!
records.summary: A tweet describes named news organizations as an enemy of the public rather than only an opponent of Trump.
records.context: The entry records his description. It does not adopt the accusation or treat criticism of reporting as an implemented censorship policy.
records.research_question: Which audience is addressed, and is any later institutional restriction separately documented?
records.date_basis: The February 17 collection includes the later 21:48:22 UTC version. Original platform ID remains to be recovered.

records.title: Conditional force warning to North Korea
records.quote: They will be met with fire and fury like the world has never seen.
records.summary: Trump warns North Korea against further threats while answering a reporter.
records.context: The statement occurs during an exchange before an opioid briefing. It is a threatened response, not documentation that a particular strike occurred.
records.research_question: What trigger, target and consequence are stated, and what actually followed?

records.title: Nuclear-capability comparison
records.quote: I too have a Nuclear Button
records.summary: Trump responds to Kim Jong Un by comparing the countries' nuclear capabilities and saying his button works.
records.context: A rhetorical comparison is not evidence of an order to launch a weapon or of a private mental condition.
records.research_question: How does a threat claim military advantage, and what response or de-escalation follows?
records.date_basis: The archive groups this at January 3, 00:49:19 UTC, corresponding to January 2 in US Eastern time.

records.title: Warning addressed to Iran's president
records.quote: NEVER EVER THREATEN THE UNITED STATES AGAIN
records.summary: Trump warns President Rouhani against threatening the United States and invokes severe consequences.
records.context: The warning has a named addressee and a stated condition. Subsequent policy and military events require their own dates and sources.
records.research_question: What action is demanded, and does the later record show the threatened consequence?
records.date_basis: The July 23 archive lists 03:24:19 UTC, corresponding to July 22 in US Eastern time.

records.title: Claim about Article II authority
records.quote: the right to do whatever I want as President
records.summary: Trump invokes Article II while discussing the Mueller investigation and obstruction allegations.
records.context: The surrounding investigation context is retained. This is a claim about presidential power, not an independent legal statement of what Article II permits.
records.research_question: What boundaries does the speaker claim, and what documents show the authority actually exercised?

records.title: Distinction between government and God
records.quote: we don't worship government, we worship God
records.summary: The same summit speech distinguishes worship of God from worship of government.
records.context: This companion passage preserves the speaker's declared standard alongside the authority claim. Whether institutions follow that standard is a separate question.
records.research_question: How does the declared object of worship compare with later demands for allegiance?

records.title: Religious praise attributed to another speaker
records.quote: like he's the King of Israel. They love him like he is the second coming of God
records.speaker: Wayne Allyn Root, quoted by Trump
records.summary: Trump publishes praise attributed to Wayne Allyn Root in a multi-part tweet sequence.
records.context: These are Root's quoted comparisons promoted by Trump's account, not words to be silently recast as an unqualified first-person claim by Trump to be God.
records.research_question: Who originates the legitimizing claim, who amplifies it, and what allegiance does it encourage?

records.title: Conditional economic threat
records.quote: I will totally destroy and obliterate the Economy of Turkey
records.summary: Trump threatens economic consequences if Turkey acts outside limits he says he will determine.
records.context: The surrounding thread concerns regional military responsibilities and captured ISIS fighters. A threatened economic consequence is not a verified record of losses or enforcement.
records.research_question: Which economic mechanism is proposed, and which dated measures implement or revise it?

records.title: Presidential authority and reopening
records.quote: the authority is total
records.summary: In a briefing about reopening, Trump describes presidential authority relative to governors as total.
records.context: He distinguishes the office from himself and qualifies the claim as concerning the subject under discussion. The transcript records the claim, not a judicial determination.
records.research_question: How does the claimed scope compare with actual orders, state responses and adjudicated limits?

records.title: Threatened intervention in Minneapolis
records.quote: I will send in the National Guard
records.summary: Trump says he will intervene if the Minneapolis mayor does not bring the city under control.
records.context: This entry uses the wording actually present in the consulted collection; a missing continuation is not reconstructed as a verified quotation.
records.research_question: What trigger and enforcement actor are identified, and which later orders can be linked?

records.title: Later explanation of shooting language
records.quote: I don't want this to happen
records.summary: Later tweets explain his earlier shooting language as a description of consequences he says he does not want.
records.context: The earlier intervention demand and later explanation remain a linked episode, not isolated evidence with the qualification removed.
records.research_question: What does the later explanation change, and what remains unresolved without the original full thread?

records.title: Invitation to January 6 protest
records.quote: Be there, will be wild!
records.summary: Trump invites supporters to a January 6 protest while asserting that the 2020 election result was wrong.
records.context: The fraud allegation is the speaker's claim, not a fact established by this tweet. A rally invitation is distinct from later actions by participants.
records.research_question: What action was requested, and how do subsequent statements alter the demand?

records.title: Pressure on the vice president
records.quote: Mike Pence didn't have the courage
records.summary: Trump criticizes Pence for not taking the electoral action he wanted.
records.context: The record concerns a public demand and response, not a new finding about legal authority or criminal liability.
records.research_question: How is expected cooperation described, and what happens when the officeholder refuses?
records.date_basis: January 6 at 14:24 Eastern, as explicitly supplied in the archive.

records.title: Call for peaceful conduct
records.quote: Stay peaceful!
records.summary: At 14:38 Eastern, Trump asks for support for Capitol Police and peaceful conduct.
records.context: This later statement remains attached to the 14:24 Pence criticism. Its wording and its practical effect are different questions.
records.research_question: What request follows the earlier criticism, and what evidence establishes its reception?

records.title: Retrospective explanation and departure request
records.quote: a sacred landslide election victory
records.summary: The 18:01 Eastern tweet invokes a supposedly deprived victory while also asking people to go home peacefully.
records.context: Both the explanatory claim and departure request belong to the same message; its election allegation is not independently validated here.
records.research_question: How does the message explain events, and what continuing action does it request?

records.title: Alleged fraud and constitutional rules
records.quote: the termination of all rules, regulations, and articles, even those found in the Constitution
records.summary: A post argues that the alleged scale of election fraud permits termination of rules, including constitutional provisions.
records.context: This records his proposed exception and underlying allegation, not proof of fraud or of an enacted suspension. The December 5 denial is linked.
records.research_question: What exception is claimed, and how does the later explanation define or revise it?

records.title: Response to the constitutional-rule controversy
records.quote: This is simply more DISINFORMATION & LIES
records.summary: Trump denies that he wanted to terminate the Constitution and says he wanted a remedy for alleged fraud.
records.context: The denial does not replace the earlier wording in the archive; both sources remain available for comparison.
records.research_question: What precisely is denied, and what remedy remains advocated?

records.title: Representation and promised retribution
records.quote: I am your retribution.
records.summary: An archived CPAC clip presents Trump as the voice, warrior and agent of justice for people described as wronged.
records.context: The clip is not a transcript of the entire event. The promise should be distinguished from a subsequent order or completed act.
records.research_question: What remedy is promised to the audience, against whom, and through what institution?

records.title: Day-one exception in a town-hall exchange
records.quote: Except for day one.
records.summary: In a Hannity town hall, Trump gives a day-one exception when asked about abuse of power and retribution.
records.context: The quoted clip continues with border closure and drilling, followed by a statement that he would not be a dictator afterward. No private intention or governing classification is inferred.
records.research_question: What actions are attached to the exception, and how does the complete exchange frame its scope?
records.date_basis: Town hall was December 5; the consulted CNN clip transcript aired December 6.

records.title: Religious narration in shared campaign media
records.quote: a shepherd to mankind who won't ever leave nor forsake them
records.speaker: Video narrator; distributed on Trump account
records.summary: A video on Trump's account portrays him through divine-caretaker and shepherd imagery.
records.context: The quoted words are the video narrator's, not a newly attributed Trump speech. The source is an archive transcript; complete-video and authorship review remain open.
records.research_question: Who makes and circulates the representation, and what authority is claimed for its subject?

records.title: Survival attributed to divine intervention
records.quote: it was God alone who prevented the unthinkable from happening
records.summary: Trump attributes his survival to God in a post after the assassination attempt.
records.context: The same message expresses concern for other victims and calls for unity. This is a documented religious interpretation by the speaker, not a verified supernatural cause.
records.research_question: How is survival narrated, and what subsequent statements attach a political mission to it?

records.title: Survival and political mission
records.quote: I was saved by God to make America great again.
records.summary: The inaugural address connects survival of the assassination attempt with a stated political mission.
records.context: The statement is Trump's theological explanation. It does not establish that an injury was fatal or that divine intervention was independently verified.
records.research_question: What mission is attached to survival, and who later repeats or institutionalizes that claim?

records.title: Stated peace-making standard
records.quote: a peacemaker and unifier
records.summary: Trump says he wants his legacy to be one of peace-making and unity.
records.context: Preserve this stated objective alongside later war statements. Whether a particular negotiation succeeded requires its own observed chronology.
records.research_question: Which later events can be compared with the speaker's own stated peace-making standard?

records.title: Saving the country and the law
records.quote: He who saves his Country does not violate any Law.
records.summary: The account posts a maxim connecting national rescue with nonviolation of law.
records.context: The short text names no specific action or legal proceeding. Neither its intended referent nor its legal validity is supplied by the post.
records.research_question: What action, if any, is later defended through this claimed exception?

records.title: Royal language in a transport-policy announcement
records.quote: LONG LIVE THE KING!
records.summary: A post celebrating the announced end of New York congestion pricing uses royal language.
records.context: The immediate subject is congestion pricing. The slogan is not itself a change in the constitutional form of government.
records.research_question: How does the representation of authority relate to the actual policy instrument and its limits?

records.title: Claim of unique negotiating ability
records.quote: only "TRUMP," and the Trump Administration, can do
records.summary: The account says it alone can negotiate an end to the Russia-Ukraine war.
records.context: The surrounding post includes allegations and numerical claims about Ukraine that are not adopted as verified facts here. The subject is the asserted indispensability.
records.research_question: What exclusivity is asserted, and how does a later agreement document the roles of other participants?

records.title: Food benefits linked to government reopening
records.quote: will be given only when the Radical Left Democrats open up government
records.summary: Trump links SNAP payments to a political action by congressional opponents.
records.context: The White House subsequently said it was complying with the court order for partial payments. Benefit eligibility, an announced funding condition and actual disbursements remain distinct.
records.research_question: Which condition controls actual food access, and is it imposed on legislators, individual recipients, or both?
